`AllNamespaces` install into a shared namespace such as `openshift-operators`, use it instead of
`node-upgrade-mutex-operator`, and keep it in step 5.

1. Make sure no run is active: every MutexRunConfig shows `Upgrade` `False` and `Paused` `False`, and
   `oc get clusterversion` shows no upgrade in progress.
2. Delete the MutexRunConfigs in every namespace while the operator still runs, so that their finalizers run. In an
   `AllNamespaces` install those outside the operator namespace carry the finalizer too; without the operator, they
   would make the CRD deletion in step 5 hang. `oc delete` waits until they are gone:

   ```sh
   oc delete mutexrunconfig --all -A
   ```

3. Delete the MutexTargets and MutexRules, and the Jobs in other namespaces:

   ```sh
   oc delete mutextarget,mutexrule --all -A
   oc get jobs -A -l nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/job-key
   oc delete jobs -A -l nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/job-key
   ```

4. Delete the Subscription and the CSV:

   ```sh
   oc delete subscriptions.operators.coreos.com --all -n node-upgrade-mutex-operator
   oc get csv -n node-upgrade-mutex-operator -o name | grep openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator |
     xargs oc delete -n node-upgrade-mutex-operator
   ```

5. Delete the CRDs, the namespace (with its OperatorGroup), and the CatalogSource if you added one. If a CRD stays
   `Terminating`, `oc get mutexrunconfig -A` shows the MutexRunConfig that still has the finalizer: restore it by hand,
   including step 4 there.

   ```sh
   oc delete crd mutexrules.nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io mutextargets.nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io \
     mutexrunconfigs.nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io
   oc delete namespace node-upgrade-mutex-operator
   oc delete catalogsource node-upgrade-mutex-operator-catalog -n openshift-marketplace
   ```

6. Delete the RBAC you created: the metrics ClusterRoleBinding, if any (see [Metrics](#metrics)); for
   `job-example.yaml`, `oc delete clusterrolebinding,clusterrole mutex-node-labeler`; for `job-wait-for-app.yaml`,
   `oc delete serviceaccount,role,rolebinding mutex-wait-for-app -n my-app`; and the ServiceAccounts and RBAC of your
   own Jobs.
7. Undo what the operator does not track: labels your Jobs left on the nodes after an abort, such as that of
   `job-example.yaml` (`oc label nodes --all example.com/pre-upgrade-done-`), and the pause of pools you
   [paused yourself](#pausing-the-pools-yourself).
8. Optional: delete the canary pool. First remove `isCanary` from any node that has it (`oc label node <node>
   isCanary-`) and wait until `oc get mcp canary` shows `MACHINECOUNT` `0`. Then `oc delete mcp canary`.
9. Optional: delete the MachineConfig `00-release-image-version`, then the NFD instance
   (`oc delete nodefeaturediscovery nfd-instance -n openshift-nfd`) and, if nothing else uses it, the NFD operator.
   **Deleting the MachineConfig reboots every node of every pool that renders the worker MachineConfigs.** Whether NFD
   removes the version label is unknown; `oc label nodes --all machineconfiguration.openshift.io/release-image-version-`
   does, once NFD is gone.
10. Check that nothing is left: `oc get nodes,mcp -o yaml | grep -c 'nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io'` prints
    `0`.

## Reference

### Labels and annotations

`<value>` is the SHA-1 of the MutexRunConfig's `<namespace>/<name>` (see the [Glossary](#glossary)).

| Key | Object | Example value | Set by | Removed by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label `mutexrule.nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/<rule>.<namespace>` | target node that is behind | `""` | the Label step | the release patch; the restore; the finalizer |
| annotation `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/labelled-by` | target node that is behind | `node-upgrade-mutex-operator/workers` | the Label step, with the mutex labels | with the mutex labels |
| label `mutexrule.nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/release` | released node | `<value>` | the release patch | the patch after its cleanup Jobs; the restore; the finalizer |
| annotation `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/released-by` | released node | see below | the release patch | with the release label |
| label `mutexrule.nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/release` | the canary's own nodes | `<value>` | the Label step, at the start of a run | a reconcile after the settle time following the restore; the finalizer |
| annotation `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/paused-by` | target pool the run paused | `node-upgrade-mutex-operator/workers` | the Pause step, with `spec.paused: true` | the restore and the finalizer, which unpause the pool |
| annotation `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/original-match-expressions` | target pools and canary | JSON of the original `matchExpressions` | the first selector change | the restore and the finalizer, which put the list back |
| annotation `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/modified-by` | target pools and canary | `node-upgrade-mutex-operator/workers` | with `original-match-expressions` | with it |
| annotation `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/release-labelled-at` | canary with nodes of its own | `2026-01-31T12:00:00Z` | the Label step, before and after the release labels change | the re-point; every restore |
| annotation `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/restored-at` | canary with nodes of its own | `2026-01-31T14:00:00Z node-upgrade-mutex-operator/workers` | the restore of the canary | after the canary's own nodes lose the release label; the finalizer |
| label `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/job-key` and the Job annotations | Jobs | a SHA-1 | Job creation | never: the operator does not delete Jobs |
| finalizer `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/finalizer` | MutexRunConfig | | ansible-operator | ansible-operator, after the restore |

The `released-by` value is the MutexRunConfig's `<namespace>/<name>`, a `|`, and the target version, for example
`node-upgrade-mutex-operator/workers|4.21.22`.

During a run the target pools' `matchExpressions` get `mutexrule.nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/release NotIn
(<value>)`, and the canary's get its kept expressions plus `... release In (<value>)`. Before the re-point, a canary
with nodes of its own has its own expressions plus one `<mutex label> DoesNotExist` per MutexRule. `matchLabels` are
never changed. A pool an administrator paused is not annotated with `paused-by` and is never unpaused. Marks of
another MutexRunConfig are left alone.

### Conditions

`lastTransitionTime` is an RFC 3339 UTC time. It changes whenever a condition's status, reason or message changes.
The messages below are quoted from the operator; `...` stands for names and values.

**Validation**

| Kind, type | Status, reason | Meaning and message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all, `Reconciled` | `False` `NamespaceNotAllowed` | "... are only reconciled in the operator namespace '...'. Nothing was done." | [Runbook](#the-cr-is-ignored-namespacenotallowed) |
| MutexRule, `ValidConfig` | `True` `ValidConfig` | "jobSpec and cleanUpJobSpec passed a server-side dry-run create of a Job in namespace ..." | Nothing. It does not check everything: see [MutexRule](#mutexrule). |
| MutexRule, `ValidConfig` | `False` `InvalidConfig` | The API server's error, or "spec.jobName is empty.", "spec.type '...' is not supported; only 'kubernetes' is." | Fix the rule. |
| MutexTarget, `ValidConfig` | `True` `MachineConfigPoolFetchSucceeded`, `False` `MachineConfigPoolFetchFailed` | The pools exist, or "MachineConfigPool(s) ... were not found." | Fix the pool names. |
| MutexTarget, `NodeListGathered` | `True` `MachineConfigPoolFetchSucceeded`, `False` `MachineConfigPoolFetchFailed` | "All nodes were successfully fetched.", or for example "MachineConfigPool ... has an empty nodeSelector." `status.nodes` is then empty. | Fix the pool's selector. |
| MutexRunConfig, `ConfigValidated` | `True` `FetchSucceeded` | "Canary, MutexRules, and MutexTargets were successfully fetched and validated (... rule(s), pool(s) ..., ... target node(s))." | Nothing. |
| MutexRunConfig, `ConfigValidated` | `False` `ValidationFailed` | The failed check. Nothing is changed. | [Runbook](#validation-fails-validatedfalse) |
| MutexRunConfig, `ConfigValidated` | `False` `ClusterStateInvalid` | "The cluster state check failed, so nothing is paused, labelled or run: ..." | [Runbook](#apiservices-are-down-clusterstateinvalid) |
| MutexRunConfig, `ClusterStateValidated` | `True` `APIServicesUp`, `False` `APIServicesDown` | "APIService condition Available is True for all APIServices", or "... is not True for ..." | As above. |

**Detection**

| Type | Status, reason | Meaning and message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `UpgradeChecked` | `True` `CheckSucceeded`, `False` `CheckFailed` | The check ran, or why not, for example "ClusterVersion status.desired.version is '...', which is not a semantic version." | Fix the cause in the message. |
| `NodeVersionsKnown` | `True` `VersionsKnown`, `False` `VersionLabelMissing` | Every target node has a valid version label, or "Target node(s) ... do not exist or have no semantic-version ... label ..." | [Runbook](#node-versions-unknown-nodeversionsknownfalse) |
| `UpgradeAvailable` | `True` `UpgradeAvailable` | "Target node(s) ... are behind ...", or "... were released by this MutexRunConfig and still need their cleanup Jobs." | Nothing: a run is due. |
| `UpgradeAvailable` | `False` `UpgradeUnavailable`, `False` `UpgradeFinished` | "All target nodes run ..." | Nothing. |
| `UpgradeReady` | `True` `UpgradeReady` | "An upgrade is available": nodes can be released. | Nothing. |
| `UpgradeReady` | `False` `UpgradeNotReady`, `False` `UpgradeFinished` | "Waiting for the control plane to complete ... (ClusterVersion history[0] is ... for ...)", or "An upgrade is not available". | Nothing. |

**Run**

| Type | Status, reason | Meaning and message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TargetPoolsPaused` | `True` `Paused`, `False` `NotPaused` | "MachineConfigPools paused by this MutexRunConfig: ...", "Target MachineConfigPools paused by someone else, which this MutexRunConfig never unpauses: ...", "No MachineConfigPool is paused by this MutexRunConfig.", or "The target Machine Config Pools could not all be paused: ..." Written at the end of a reconcile. | Unpause a pool paused by someone else yourself after the run. |
| `MutexRulesApplied` | `True` `ApplySucceeded`, `False` `ApplyFailed` | "MutexRule labels are applied to the ... target node(s) behind ...", or the error. | On `False`, see the error; the run is retried. |
| `MCPUpdated` | `True` `UpdateSucceeded` | "MachineConfigPools ... were successfully updated for the run." | Nothing. |
| `MCPUpdated` | `False` `CanaryMembersLabelled` | The canary's own nodes' release label changed less than the settle time ago, so the pools are re-pointed at a later reconcile, normally the next one. | Nothing: wait. |
| `MCPUpdated` | `False` `UpdateFailed` | "MachineConfigPools was not successfully updated: ..." | See the error; the run is retried. |
| `JobRun` | `True` `JobRunSucceeded` | "Jobs for ... have run successfully." with "Node is i of n". | Nothing. |
| `JobRun` | `False` `JobRunFailed` | The node, its position and the error: "... failed: ...", "... did not finish within ...s (timeoutSeconds)", or "... could not be read: ...". | [Runbook](#a-job-failed-jobrunfailed) |
| `NodeUpgrade` | `True` `NodeUpgradeSucceeded`, `True` `NodeAlreadyUpgraded` | "Upgrade for ... has run successfully." with "Node is i of n", or "... already runs ... and has no Jobs left to run." | Nothing. |
| `NodeUpgrade` | `False` `NodeUpgradeFailed` | The node did not finish its upgrade in time and what it lacks, or MCO started updating another target node. | [Runbook](#a-node-did-not-finish-its-upgrade-nodeupgradefailed) |

**Finish and report**

| Type | Status, reason | Meaning and message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MCPUpdated` | `False` `SelectorsRestored` | "The original node selectors of ... were restored." | Nothing. |
| `UpgradeAvailable`, `UpgradeReady` | `False` `UpgradeFinished` | "All target nodes run ..." | Nothing. |
| `Degraded` | `True` `PoolsLeftPaused` | A step failed while this MutexRunConfig holds pools paused or re-pointed. The message names the pools and the error and, unless it is being deleted, how to abort. Written at the end of a reconcile. | [Troubleshooting and recovery](#troubleshooting-and-recovery) |
| `Degraded` | `False` `RunInProgress` | "... are paused while the upgrade to ... is in progress." | Watch the run. |
| `Degraded` | `False` `NoPoolsPaused` | "No MachineConfigPool is paused by this MutexRunConfig." After a failure it adds "Last error: ...". | Read the last error. |

### Reconcile procedure

**MutexRule:** checks the type and fields, sends `jobSpec` and `cleanUpJobSpec` as server-side dry-run creates
(`dryRun=All`) to the job namespace, and reports `ValidConfig`. Nothing is created or deleted.

**MutexTarget:** checks that the pools exist, computes their nodes from `matchLabels` and `matchExpressions`, and
reports `ValidConfig`, `NodeListGathered` and `status.nodes`. During a run it uses the saved original selectors.

**MutexRunConfig:** each step lists the condition it writes and when it runs.

1. **Namespace.** Outside the operator namespace: `Reconciled=False NamespaceNotAllowed`, and nothing else, also on
   delete.
2. **Resolve references.** Default the reference namespaces; build the label keys and the release value. Always.
3. **Finalize.** Only when the MutexRunConfig is being deleted: read the MutexTargets still present, run the Restore
   (step 10), and stop. No validation and no Jobs.
4. **Validate** (`ConfigValidated`, `ClusterStateValidated`). Always. References, rules, targets and canary as in
   [Validation fails](#validation-fails-validatedfalse), then every APIService must be `Available` (3 checks, 10 s
   apart). Read-only.
5. **Check for an upgrade** (`UpgradeChecked`, `NodeVersionsKnown`, `UpgradeAvailable`, `UpgradeReady`). When
   validation passed. The target version is `status.desired.version`. A node is behind when its version label is
   lower. `UpgradeAvailable` is also `True` while a node this run released still needs its cleanup Jobs, for any
   version. `UpgradeReady` is `True` once, in addition, `status.history[0]` is `Completed` for the target version.
6. **Pause** (`TargetPoolsPaused` on failure). When the check passed and an upgrade is available. Pools that are not
   paused get `spec.paused: true` and `paused-by`. A pool that is already paused is used as it is.
7. **Label** (`MutexRulesApplied`). After the pause. Every node that is behind gets the mutex labels and
   `labelled-by`, and loses any release label, except nodes already released by this run and nodes MCO is already
   updating through the canary. The released nodes and the canary's own nodes get this run's release value; every
   other node loses it. When this changes the canary's membership before the re-point, the canary first gets the hold
   selector and `release-labelled-at`.
8. **Re-point** (`MCPUpdated`). After the labels. The canary first, then the target pools, after saving their
   expressions in `original-match-expressions` with `modified-by`. MCO resets the selector of its `worker` pool at
   once, so on `worker` the `NotIn` expression does not stay; there MCO's own rule keeps a node that matches a custom
   pool (the canary, once the node has the release label) out of `worker`. Deferred while `release-labelled-at` is
   younger than the settle time (`CanaryMembersLabelled`).
9. **Run, node by node** (`JobRun`, `NodeUpgrade`). When `UpgradeReady`, and the pause, labels and re-point
   succeeded. Nodes this run already released come first and resume at the wait. Target nodes MCO is already updating
   come next: the operator first waits, up to 2 hours, until MCO reports each `Done` and `Ready`; a node that was
   behind still gets its pre-upgrade Jobs. Then the rest, as in [The Job contract](#the-job-contract). Any failure,
   also MCO starting on another target node, stops the run; the remaining nodes are not touched.
10. **Restore** (`MCPUpdated=False SelectorsRestored`; `UpgradeFinished` after a full run). When validation and the
    check passed, and either every node was processed or no upgrade is available (which also cleans up the leftovers
    of an earlier run). Selectors first, the canary last; then the run's labels and node annotations; then the pools
    this MutexRunConfig paused are unpaused. The canary's own nodes keep the release label until a later reconcile.
11. **Report** (`TargetPoolsPaused`, `Degraded`). Always, also after a failure.

A MutexRunConfig is reconciled when its spec changes, when one of its Jobs in its own namespace changes, and every 10
minutes. Changes to ClusterVersion, nodes, pools or MutexRules are picked up at the next reconcile. Status is merged
condition by condition, so progress survives a restart of the operator.

### Timings

| What | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Reconcile period of every CR | 10 minutes |
| Noticing a new upgrade | at the next reconcile, at most 10 minutes later (ClusterVersion is not watched) |
| Settle time | 300 seconds |
| Job check | every 10 seconds, for up to the MutexRule's `spec.timeoutSeconds` (default 3600) per Job and attempt |
| Node upgrade wait, and the wait for an update MCO already started | every 60 seconds, 120 times: 2 hours per node |
| APIService check | 3 checks, 10 seconds apart |
| Retry after a failed reconcile | a few milliseconds at first, doubling up to about 17 minutes (controller-runtime's default backoff) |

`timeoutSeconds` is set in each MutexRule. The other values are built into the operator image (in the source:
[watches.yaml](watches.yaml) and the [role defaults](roles/mutexrunconfig/defaults/main.yml)).

#### Why some steps wait 5 minutes

This applies only when the canary has nodes of its own. MCO's controller can work from an old view of the nodes:
after an API outage it saw the nodes again 70 to 115 seconds after the API was back in the live runs, and rendered
their pools about 2 minutes after it. A selector change that depends on a release label must not reach MCO before the
label does, or MCO could move a node into the wrong pool. So:

* **At the start of a run** the canary's own nodes get the release label. The operator records the time in the
  canary's `release-labelled-at` annotation before the label changes, and again after the last one. Meanwhile the
  canary selects with its own expressions plus `<mutex label> DoesNotExist` per MutexRule, so the held nodes stay out.
  The pools are re-pointed only at a later reconcile at least 300 seconds after that time, never the one that wrote
  it, normally the next one 10 minutes later. Until then `MCPUpdated=False CanaryMembersLabelled`. The time is kept
  in the cluster, so a retry or a restart of the operator waits too.
* **At the end of a run** the restore of the canary records the time in its `restored-at` annotation. The nodes keep
  the release label until a reconcile at least 300 seconds later, normally about 10 minutes after the run, and then
  the annotation goes too. A reconcile right after the run, such as one its last Jobs trigger, keeps them.

With an empty canary neither wait happens, and the pools are re-pointed at once. Two gaps remain. An API outage that
begins right after the time is recorded and lasts longer than 5 minutes, followed by MCO's delay, can still move one
of the canary's own nodes through the `worker` pool once (unpaused when `worker` is not a target pool). The finalizer
has a single pass: it removes the label right after it restores the canary, so an MCO view that lags the restore can
do the same once.

### One MutexRunConfig at a time

The operator reconciles MutexRunConfigs one at a time (the argument `--max-concurrent-reconciles=1` of its
Deployment, which applies to each kind). While one MutexRunConfig works through its nodes, no other is
reconciled: their periodic reconciles, retries and finalizers wait, and their status is not updated. MutexRules and
MutexTargets have workers of their own and are not held up. In practice:

* Several MutexRunConfigs upgrade their nodes one after another, so plan for the sum of their runs. One that has
  already paused its pools keeps them paused while it waits.
* A MutexRunConfig created or changed during another one's run is validated, and pauses its pools, only after that run.
* Deleting a MutexRunConfig while another one works through its nodes takes effect only after that whole run. To
  abort sooner, [restore by hand](#restore-by-hand).
* Do not start another OpenShift upgrade while a run is in progress (see
  [the runbook](#a-second-openshift-upgrade-started-during-a-run)).

### Retries

ansible-operator counts every failed task as a failed reconcile, also one the role handles and reports in a
condition. A failed reconcile is retried with controller-runtime's backoff, not at the 10-minute period: first after
a few milliseconds, then doubling up to about 17 minutes between attempts, until a reconcile succeeds. This applies to
every failure the conditions report. A failed Job is started again on every retry.

### Permissions

The operator's ServiceAccount gets these permissions cluster-wide, as the CSV's `spec.install.spec.clusterPermissions`
list them (source: [config/rbac/](config/rbac/)):

| API group | Resource | Verbs | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `batch` | `jobs` | create, get, list, watch | Dry-run validation, creating MutexRule Jobs and following them. Never deleted, patched or updated. |
| core | `nodes` | get, list, watch, patch | Reading versions, pool membership, the MCO state and `Ready`. Adding and removing the mutex labels, the release label, and the `labelled-by` and `released-by` annotations. |
| `machineconfiguration.openshift.io` | `machineconfigpools` | get, list, watch, patch | Reading selectors. Pausing, unpausing, changing `matchExpressions` and the five pool annotations. |
| `config.openshift.io` | `clusterversions` | get, list, watch | The target version and the control plane's progress. |
| `apiregistration.k8s.io` | `apiservices` | get, list, watch | The APIService check. |
| `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io` | `mutexrules`, `mutextargets`, `mutexrunconfigs` | get, list, watch, update, patch | Watching and reading the CRs. Adding and removing the finalizer. |
| `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io` | `mutexrules/status`, `mutextargets/status`, `mutexrunconfigs/status` | get, update, patch | Writing status. |
| `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io` | `mutexrules/finalizers`, `mutexrunconfigs/finalizers` | update | Lets Jobs carry owner references with `blockOwnerDeletion`. Not used today; kept as in the operator-sdk scaffold. |
| `authentication.k8s.io` | `tokenreviews` | create | Authenticating scrapes of the metrics endpoint. |
| `authorization.k8s.io` | `subjectaccessreviews` | create | Authorizing scrapes of the metrics endpoint. |

For leader election it also gets `coordination.k8s.io` `leases` (all verbs) and `events` (create, patch) in its own
namespace (the CSV's `spec.install.spec.permissions`). With an `AllNamespaces` install, OLM grants these namespaced
permissions cluster-wide and adds get, list and watch on `namespaces`.

### Metrics

The manager serves `/metrics` over HTTPS on port 8443, behind the Service
`openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator-metrics-service` in the operator namespace. A scrape must send a bearer token
whose identity may `get` the `/metrics` URL. The ClusterRole `openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator-metrics-reader`
grants that. Bind it to the ServiceAccount that scrapes, for example:

```sh
oc create clusterrolebinding mutex-operator-metrics-reader \
  --clusterrole=openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator-metrics-reader \
  --serviceaccount=<scraper-namespace>:<scraper-serviceaccount>
```

The binding is accepted even when the ClusterRole name is wrong, and every scrape then gets `403 Forbidden`, so copy
the name exactly.

## Moving from 0.2.x

0.3.0 is a new API. Its group is `nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io` (0.2.x used `openshift-optional.skrzypek.io`),
and so are its node labels, pool and node annotations and finalizer. 0.3.0 does not read 0.2.x CRs, labels or
annotations, so the project's catalog starts afresh and offers no upgrade from 0.2.x, nor from 0.3.0-rc1, a
pre-release published only from the old repository with the old group. Move by reinstalling: save the CRs, uninstall
the old version, install 0.3.0, and create the CRs again under the new group.

The 0.2.x images are hosted in a registry that no longer exists, so 0.2.x can no longer be installed, and a 0.2.x
operator pod that has to pull its image again cannot start. The community catalogs hold only 0.2.x. If one of them
ever offers 0.3.0 as an upgrade of 0.2.x, do not approve it (set the Subscription to `Manual` approval first).

What changes for the CRs you create again:

* **Only CRs in the operator namespace are reconciled.** 0.2.x reconciled CRs in every namespace. References to
  MutexRules or MutexTargets in another namespace fail validation.
* **`SingleNamespace` is no longer supported.** Use `OwnNamespace` (the console's default for a namespace of its own)
  or `AllNamespaces`.
* **The CRDs validate their fields.** Every kind needs `spec`. A MutexRule needs `jobName`, a DNS-1123 label of at
  most 52 characters, and `jobSpec`; `jobNamespace`, when set, must be a DNS-1123 label. A MutexTarget needs at least
  one pool. A MutexRunConfig needs `canary.name` and at least one rule and one target reference, each with a `name`;
  rule names (at most 61 characters) and every reference `namespace` must be DNS-1123 labels.
* **The canary must not reach other nodes** (see [The canary pool](#the-canary-pool)). With a custom target pool and
  the sample canary, `ConfigValidated` stays `False` until the canary gets an expression such as
  `node-role.kubernetes.io/app Exists`.
* **Jobs can take longer.** 0.2.x stopped the run when a Job had not completed within 2 minutes. 0.3.0 waits up to the
  rule's `spec.timeoutSeconds`, 3600 by default.

To move:

1. Choose a time when no OpenShift upgrade is in progress and no 0.2.x run is half done. 0.2.x has no finalizer and
   does not record what it changed, so nothing can finish or undo a 0.2.x run after it is uninstalled. No target pool
   should be paused, except by you, and this must print nothing:

   ```sh
   oc get nodes,mcp -o yaml | grep 'openshift-optional.skrzypek.io/'
   ```

   If it prints labels, annotations or `matchExpressions`, let the run finish, or put the pools' original
   `matchExpressions` back, remove the labels and unpause the pools by hand.
2. Save the 0.2.x CRs, in every namespace:

   ```sh
   oc get mutexrules.openshift-optional.skrzypek.io,mutextargets.openshift-optional.skrzypek.io,mutexrunconfigs.openshift-optional.skrzypek.io -A -o yaml > mutex-0.2.x.yaml
   ```

3. Uninstall 0.2.x: delete its Subscription and CSV, then its CRDs, which also deletes the 0.2.x CRs (0.2.x has no
   finalizer, so nothing hangs). The 0.3.0-rc1 pre-release puts the finalizer `openshift-optional.skrzypek.io/finalizer`
   on every MutexRunConfig: for rc1, first delete them all while the rc1 operator still runs, and wait until they are
   gone (`oc delete` waits), so its finalizer restores what it changed:

   ```sh
   oc delete mutexrunconfigs.openshift-optional.skrzypek.io --all -A     # rc1 only
   oc delete subscriptions.operators.coreos.com <name> -n <operator namespace>
   oc delete csv <0.2.x CSV name> -n <operator namespace>
   oc delete crd mutexrules.openshift-optional.skrzypek.io mutextargets.openshift-optional.skrzypek.io mutexrunconfigs.openshift-optional.skrzypek.io
   ```

   Without a running rc1 operator the first delete hangs. Once the command in step 1 prints nothing, remove the
   finalizer from each: `oc patch mutexrunconfigs.openshift-optional.skrzypek.io <name> -n <namespace> --type=merge
   -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}'`.

4. Install 0.3.0 as described in [Install](#install). If the 0.2.x OperatorGroup targets another namespace
   (`SingleNamespace`), make it `OwnNamespace` first.
5. Create the CRs again from `mutex-0.2.x.yaml`, with `apiVersion: nodeupgrade.redhat-na-ssa.github.io/v1alpha1`, in
   the operator namespace, without `status` and the server-set `metadata` fields, and checked against the rules above.
   Start from the [sample manifests](sample-manifests/README.md).
6. Afterwards `oc get mutexrunconfig -n <operator namespace>` must show every MutexRunConfig as `Validated` `True`.
   Fix any that is not before the next OpenShift upgrade: a MutexRunConfig that fails validation pauses nothing.

This procedure has not yet been run as written (see [tests/Scenarios.md](tests/Scenarios.md)).

## Development

The operator is an [operator-sdk](https://sdk.operatorframework.io/) Ansible operator. `watches.yaml` maps each custom
resource to a role in `roles/`, and the image is `quay.io/operator-framework/ansible-operator:v1.42.3` plus the
collections in `requirements.yml` (`kubernetes.core`, `operator_sdk.util`). This part is for maintainers. Read it with
[DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md), which explains the reconcile pipeline, the state the operator keeps in the cluster and what it
assumes about the Machine Config Operator (MCO). [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the short version for
contributors.

`PROJECT` is operator-sdk's project file, `playbooks/` holds only a placeholder, and `LICENSE` is Apache-2.0.

### Tools you need

| To run | You need |
| --- | --- |
| `make lint` | Python with `yamllint`, `ansible-core` 2.18 and `ansible-lint`. CI pins `yamllint==1.38.0`, `ansible-core==2.18.18` and `ansible-lint==26.9.0`. The first run needs network access (see Running and testing). |
| `shellcheck hack/*.sh` | `shellcheck` |
| `make docs-lint`, `make diagrams-check` | `bash` 3.2 or later, `git`, `awk`, `grep`, `sort`, and `sha256sum` or `shasum` |
| `make diagrams` | podman, or docker with `CONTAINER_TOOL=docker` (not tested). It pulls the pinned mermaid-cli image, about 2.4 GB. |
| `make document`, `make bundle`, `make verify-manifests`, the catalog targets | `make`, `curl`, `sed` and `awk` (GNU or BSD); the Makefile downloads the rest |
| `make docker-build`, `make image-smoke-test` and the other image targets | podman (the default `CONTAINER_TOOL`) or docker |
| `make install`, `make deploy`, `make run` | `kubectl` and a cluster in your kubeconfig. Only an OpenShift cluster has the MachineConfigPool and ClusterVersion APIs the operator needs. |
| `molecule test -s kind` | Python, `pip install -r molecule/requirements.txt`, kind, and docker or podman ([molecule/README.md](molecule/README.md)) |
| `make release` | a login to the registry in `IMAGE_TAG_BASE`; `skopeo` to record a bundle by digest |

The Makefile downloads its other tools into `./bin` at pinned versions: operator-sdk v1.42.3, kustomize v5.8.3 and yq
v4.54.1. The ansible-operator and opm versions are read from the `FROM` lines of `Dockerfile` and `catalog.Dockerfile`.
To use your own binary, pass its path, for example `make bundle OPM=/usr/local/bin/opm`. Building needs no registry
login: the base images are public, and nothing comes from `registry.redhat.io`.

### Version and registry

`.envrc` holds the release settings: `MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, `IMAGE_TAG_BASE`
(`ghcr.io/redhat-na-ssa/openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator`), `IMAGE_SOURCE` (this repository's URL, which the
`org.opencontainers.image.source` label on the images uses to link the `ghcr.io` packages to it), and
`USE_IMAGE_DIGESTS=true`, which pins the operator image by digest in the bundle. [direnv](https://direnv.net) exports
them. Without direnv the Makefile still reads the version from `.envrc`, but `IMAGE_TAG_BASE` falls back to the
placeholder `example.com/openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator`, which `make release` refuses, `IMAGE_SOURCE` to empty
(no label), and `USE_IMAGE_DIGESTS` to `false`, so the bundle references the operator image by tag. Pass them, for
example `make release IMAGE_TAG_BASE=<registry>/openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator USE_IMAGE_DIGESTS=true`. Set
`IMAGE_TAG_BASE` to a registry you can push to before you push anything.

The repository URL that the docs and the CSV link to is `REPO_URL` in the Makefile, and only there. `.envrc` does not
set it, so `make document` writes the same files on every machine. The release workflow sets `IMAGE_TAG_BASE`,
`IMAGE_SOURCE` and `REPO_URL` from the repository it runs in (see Releasing).

### Make targets

`make` on its own prints this list (`make help`).

| Target | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `help` | Prints the targets with their descriptions. It is the default goal. |
| `all` | The same as `docker-build`. |
| `lint` | `yamllint` (with `hack/yamllint.yaml`), `ansible-lint roles/`, and `ansible-lint` on `molecule/` with `molecule/.ansible-lint`. |
| `document` | Regenerates `README.md` (a banner, `docs/USAGE.md`, then `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`) and, from `docs/USAGE.md`, the CSV `spec.description` with links to `main`. It also sets the CSV's repository annotation and repository link from `REPO_URL`. |
| `document-check` | Runs `document`, then fails if `README.md` or the CSV base differ from what is committed. |
| `docs-lint` | Checks the Markdown files: links, anchors, alt text, the console rules for `docs/USAGE.md`, this targets table, diagram embeds, repository owners and private addresses. |
| `diagrams` | Renders `docs/diagrams/*.mmd` to `.svg` with the pinned mermaid-cli image and stamps each SVG with its source hash. |
| `diagrams-check` | Fails if an SVG is missing, has no `.mmd`, or was not rendered from its current `.mmd`, `mermaid.json` and image. Needs no container. |
| `run` | Runs ansible-operator locally against the cluster in your kubeconfig, with `watches.yaml` and one reconcile at a time per kind, as in `config/manager/manager.yaml`. |
| `docker-build` / `docker-push` | Builds or pushes the operator image `IMG` (default `$(IMAGE_TAG_BASE):$(VERSION)`). |
| `docker-buildx` | Builds and pushes a multi-arch image for `PLATFORMS`. |
| `image-smoke-test` | Checks a built image without a cluster: the license file and label, collections, Python libraries, and a syntax check of every role. |
| `install` / `uninstall` | Applies or deletes the CRDs. |
| `deploy` / `undeploy` | Applies or deletes `config/default` with `IMG`. |
| `bundle` | Generates and validates `bundles/<VERSION>/` (manifests, metadata, scorecard tests, `bundle.Dockerfile`). The bundle's CSV description links to `BUNDLE_DOCS_REF`, by default the tag `v<VERSION>`. |
| `verify-manifests` | Checks the default, manifests and testing overlays, and the bundle CSV, for known regressions. |
| `bundle-validate` | `operator-sdk bundle validate` with the optional `operatorframework` suite. |
| `bundle-build` / `bundle-push` | Builds or pushes the bundle image `BUNDLE_IMG`. |
| `catalog-add` | Adds `BUNDLE_REF` to `catalog-template.yaml` as the new head of the `alpha` channel. |
| `catalog-render` | Renders the template into `catalog/` (pulls every bundle image) and validates it. |
| `catalog-reset` | Starts a fresh catalog: keeps only the package entry in the template and in `catalog/`. |
| `catalog-validate` | Validates `catalog/` and checks that it matches the template, without pulling images. |
| `catalog-build` / `catalog-push` | Builds or pushes the catalog image `CATALOG_IMG`. |
| `release-check` | Refuses the placeholder registry, and a `VERSION` that is already in the catalog. |
| `release` | The whole release (see Releasing). |
| `latest` | Tags and pushes the three images of `VERSION` as `:latest`. |
| `increment` | Bumps `PATCH` in `.envrc`. |
| `kustomize`, `ansible-operator`, `operator-sdk`, `opm`, `yq` | Download that tool into `./bin` at its pinned version. |

`make bundle` and `make deploy` run `kustomize edit set image` in `config/manager`, which changes
`config/manager/kustomization.yaml`. Do not commit that change unless you mean to.

### Documentation and diagrams

Edit the files under `docs/`, never `README.md`. `make document` builds `README.md` from `docs/USAGE.md` and this
file, and the CSV `spec.description` from `docs/USAGE.md`. Run it after every change to those two files, and commit
`README.md` and the CSV base with your change. The other documents are read on GitHub only.

`docs/USAGE.md` is also shown in the OpenShift console, which drops some Markdown. In that file:

- no blockquotes and no GitHub alerts (lines that start with `>`);
- no h5 or h6 headings; use h2 to h4;
- no raw HTML such as `<img>`, `<details>` or `<br>`;
- every diagram is followed by a text equivalent that stands on its own, because the console shows only a link.

In every Markdown file:

- link to repository files with relative paths from the file's own directory, never with an absolute
  `github.com/.../blob/` URL. `make document` rewrites the links for `README.md` and makes them absolute in the CSV;
- keep headings ASCII, so the anchors are predictable;
- use backtick fences, not `~~~`, and no `[^1]` footnotes.

Embed a diagram on one line, with alt text that says what it shows:

```markdown
![<what the diagram shows, in one sentence>](diagrams/<name>.svg)

In words:

1. ...
```

From a role README the path is `../../docs/diagrams/<name>.svg`. Do not use GitHub's `mermaid` code blocks, `<img>`
or `<picture>`.

To change a diagram:

1. Edit `docs/diagrams/<name>.mmd`. Start it with `accTitle:` and `accDescr:`, use the real names of labels,
   annotations and conditions, and do not let a colour carry meaning alone.
2. Run `make diagrams`. It renders every `.mmd` with a white background and appends a
   `diagram-source-sha256` stamp to each SVG.
3. Commit the `.mmd` and the `.svg` together. If the diagram is embedded in `docs/USAGE.md` or this file, run
   `make document` and commit its output too.

Pitfalls met while drawing the current diagrams:

- `;` ends a statement in a sequence diagram, and a state description that ends with `:` does not parse.
- Write `<` and `>` in labels as `#lt;` and `#gt;`.
- A stadium node `([...])` adds about 30 KB of drawn path to the SVG; use a rounded node `("...")`.
- A sequence note that spans every participant widens the whole diagram once one of its lines passes about 45
  characters.
- Invisible subgraphs (`classDef row fill:none,stroke:none`) keep rows in a fixed order, as in `pool-membership.mmd`.
- Each `.mmd` sets its own `themeCSS` in its front matter, for example opaque edge-label backgrounds. Moving it into
  `mermaid.json` would change every stamp.

CI runs three checks. Run them before you open a pull request:

- `make docs-lint` checks links, anchors, alt text, the console rules, this file's targets table, that every SVG is
  embedded somewhere, that repository URLs use the owner of `REPO_URL` (except in `docs/HANDOFF.md`), and that no
  private address or host name is in a `.md` or `.mmd` file.
- `make diagrams-check` checks the stamps, so it needs no container.
- `make document-check` fails if `README.md` or the CSV base are not what `make document` writes.

The mermaid-cli image is pinned by digest in `MMDC_IMG` in the Makefile. To update it, read the new digest with
`skopeo inspect --raw docker://ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli:<version> | sha256sum`, set `MMDC_IMG` to
`ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli@sha256:<digest>`, run `make diagrams` and commit every SVG. A new digest
or any change to `mermaid.json` invalidates every stamp.

### Running and testing

- **Lint:** `make lint`. `ansible-lint` installs `requirements.yml` into `./.ansible/collections` (git-ignored), so
  the first run needs network access. Both runs use the repository root as the project directory; that is why the
  molecule run passes `--project-dir .`. With `--offline` nothing is installed, and the collections must already be
  in your collections path. Run `shellcheck hack/*.sh` for the scripts.
- **`make run`:** runs the roles from `roles/` on your machine against the cluster in your kubeconfig. Your machine
  then needs what the image has: ansible-core 2.18, ansible-runner, the Python `kubernetes` library and the
  collections in `requirements.yml`. This was not tried for this guide. `make run` sets neither `WATCH_NAMESPACE` nor
  `POD_NAMESPACE`, so every namespace is watched and allowed. Export `POD_NAMESPACE=<namespace>` first to test the
  namespace boundary. Run `make install` first to apply the CRDs.
- **`make deploy`:** `make docker-build docker-push deploy IMG=<image>` deploys `config/default`, which puts the
  operator in the namespace `openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator-system` (`config/default/kustomization.yaml`). The
  operator then acts only on CRs in that namespace. The docs and samples use `node-upgrade-mutex-operator`, so CRs
  applied from them get `Reconciled=False` (`NamespaceNotAllowed`). Create the CRs in
  `openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator-system` instead.
- **Molecule `default` on a cluster:** it refuses a cluster where the operator is installed in any way: its prepare,
  converge and destroy stop when an operator CRD lacks the label its converge sets, or when a MutexRule, MutexTarget
  or MutexRunConfig exists outside its test namespaces (`molecule/default/tasks/olm_guard.yml`). Run it on a fresh
  cluster, or run `make undeploy` (after `make deploy`) or `make uninstall` first. Both delete the CRDs, and with them
  every MutexRule, MutexTarget and MutexRunConfig in the cluster. Delete the MutexRunConfigs first, while the operator
  still runs: their finalizer restores the pools and nodes, and without the operator it never completes, so the CRD
  deletion waits.
- **Molecule `kind`:** the full simulated upgrade on a throwaway kind cluster, the same steps as the E2E job. From the
  repository root:

  ```sh
  python -m pip install -r molecule/requirements.txt
  make kustomize
  export KUSTOMIZE_PATH=$PWD/bin/kustomize-v5.8.3
  molecule test -s kind          # podman; add CONTAINER_TOOL=docker for docker
  ```

  It takes about 15 to 18 minutes in CI. Rootless podman needs cgroup v2 with the `cpu` controller delegated to the
  user. [molecule/README.md](molecule/README.md) has the variables and how the scenario fakes OpenShift, and
  [tests/Scenarios.md](tests/Scenarios.md) what each scenario covers and what only a live cluster can show.
- **Scorecard:** `operator-sdk scorecard bundles/<VERSION>` runs the `basic` and `olm` suites against a cluster.

### Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/ci.yaml` runs on every pull request and on pushes to `main`. It has read-only permissions, uses no
secrets and pushes nothing. Each job takes about a minute.

- **Lint:** `make lint`, `shellcheck hack/*.sh`, `make diagrams-check` and `make docs-lint`.
- **Build and validate**, with podman and `IMAGE_TAG_BASE=localhost/...`: `document-check`, `docker-build`,
  `image-smoke-test`, `bundle` with `bundle-validate`, `verify-manifests`, `bundle-build`, `catalog-validate` and
  `catalog-build`.

`.github/workflows/e2e.yaml` (job **Molecule on kind**) runs the molecule `kind` scenario with docker. It runs on
demand (`workflow_dispatch`) and on pull requests that touch `roles/`, `watches.yaml`, `Dockerfile`,
`requirements.yml`, `config/`, `molecule/`, `sample-manifests/` or the workflow itself. It has a 45-minute limit and
takes about 15 to 18 minutes.

`.github/workflows/release.yaml` runs only when a `v*` tag is pushed (see Releasing). It is the only workflow that
pushes anything, and it uses the workflow's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`contents: write`, `packages: write`), no other
secret.

Make **Lint** and **Build and validate** required checks in the branch protection of `main`. Do not require
**Molecule on kind**: it is path-filtered, so a pull request that does not touch those paths never gets the check, and
a required check that never runs blocks the merge.

### Releasing

![How docs and diagrams are generated and checked, and how a tag becomes the operator, bundle and catalog images and a catalog pull request.](docs/diagrams/release-pipeline.svg)

In words:

1. Docs: `make document` writes `README.md` and the CSV description (links to `main`), and `make diagrams` renders the
   SVGs with a source stamp. CI checks both with `document-check`, `diagrams-check` and `docs-lint`.
2. A maintainer merges a pull request that sets the version in `.envrc`, then tags `v<VERSION>` (or
   `v<VERSION>-rcN`) on the default branch and pushes the tag.
3. `release.yaml` checks the tag: a semver tag, its version without the suffix equal to `.envrc`, a commit of the
   default branch, and the same `.github/workflows` as the default branch.
4. `make release` builds and pushes the operator image, generates the bundle (the operator image pinned by digest, the
   description's links pinned to the tag), pushes the bundle image, adds the bundle to `catalog-template.yaml` as the
   new channel head (it replaces the old head and carries a `skipRange` from `0.3.0-rc2`), renders `catalog/`, and
   pushes the catalog image. Only a final release then moves the `:latest` tags.
5. The workflow pushes the catalog update to the branch `release/<tag>`. The maintainer opens the pull request from
   the link in the run summary and merges it before the next tag, then updates the docs for the new version
   ([After each release](#after-each-release)).
6. After a final release, a pull request bumps the version with `make increment`.
7. On the first release, the maintainer checks that the three `ghcr.io` packages are public. Publishing in the
   community catalogs is optional and done by hand.

The catalog's source of truth is `catalog-template.yaml`, an opm basic template that lists every released bundle and
the upgrade edges of the `alpha` channel. `catalog/openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator/catalog.yaml` is rendered
from it. The catalog was started afresh for this repository (`make catalog-reset`) and holds only the package entry,
so nothing can be installed from it yet. Until the first release `catalog-validate` only checks that the two files
match, since opm refuses a channel without a bundle, and `catalog-build` builds nothing. The first release from this
repository is `v0.3.0-rc2`. A `0.3.0-rc1` with the old API group was published only from the old repository; it is
not in this catalog and should not be installed. Older versions are not in it either: 0.1.x and 0.2.x use the old API
group, and their images were on a registry that is gone. Every `skipRange` starts at `CATALOG_SKIP_FROM=0.3.0-rc2`,
the first version released with the current API group, so there is no upgrade edge from 0.2.x or from `0.3.0-rc1`.
Moving from them is a reinstall ([Moving from 0.2.x](docs/USAGE.md#moving-from-02x)). The range must not start at
`0.3.0-0`, which sorts before `0.3.0-rc1`. For `v0.3.0-rc2` itself the range is `>=0.3.0-rc2 <0.3.0-rc2`, which
matches nothing.

**With the release workflow** (`.github/workflows/release.yaml`):

1. Set `MAJOR`, `MINOR` and `PATCH` in `.envrc` in a pull request and merge it. The version must not be in
   `catalog-template.yaml` yet. For `v0.3.0-rc2`, `.envrc` already says `0.3.0`.
2. Tag a commit of the default branch and push the tag, for example
   `git fetch origin && git tag v0.3.0-rc2 origin/main && git push origin v0.3.0-rc2`. A pre-release suffix must be a
   valid semver pre-release, the version without it must match `.envrc` and must not be released yet, and the `:latest`
   tags are not moved. The workflow refuses, before it publishes anything, a tag on a commit that is not on the
   default branch or whose `.github/workflows` differ from it: `GITHUB_TOKEN` could not push the catalog branch then.
3. The workflow runs `make release` with
   `IMAGE_TAG_BASE=ghcr.io/<repository owner>/openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator`, `IMAGE_SOURCE` and `REPO_URL`
   set to the repository, and `USE_IMAGE_DIGESTS=true`, logged in to `ghcr.io` with its `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The run takes
   about a minute.
4. It pushes the updated `catalog-template.yaml` and `catalog/` to the branch `release/<tag>`, and the run's summary
   links a new pull request from that branch into the default branch. Open it and merge it before you push the next
   tag.
5. Update the docs for the new version, as in [After each release](#after-each-release).
6. After a final release (not after a pre-release), run `make increment` and merge that change in a pull request.
7. On the first release, check that clusters can pull the images without a pull secret, for example
   `podman pull --authfile /dev/null ghcr.io/redhat-na-ssa/openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator-catalog:v0.3.0-rc2`.
   The three packages (`openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator`, `-bundle`, `-catalog`) are created under the
   repository owner by the first push, linked to the repository by the image label, and take the repository's
   visibility. If a package is private, make it public once (package settings, Danger Zone, Change visibility; this
   cannot be undone).
8. Write the release notes by hand. The workflow creates no GitHub Release and the repository has no changelog.

Rules that follow from how the workflow and the catalog work:

- **Merge the `release/<tag>` pull request before the next tag.** The next release starts from the template on the
  default branch. A version whose pull request was not merged is missing from that template, so it drops out of the
  next catalog image.
- **A pre-release stays in `alpha`.** `v0.3.0-rc2` becomes the head of the `alpha` channel. The final `v0.3.0`
  replaces it, and its `skipRange` (`>=0.3.0-rc2 <0.3.0`) lets clusters on any pre-release from rc2 on upgrade straight
  to it. The pre-release stays in the template. Pre-release names compare as text, so `0.3.0-rc10` sorts before
  `0.3.0-rc2` and falls outside that range: keep the number of a pre-release below 10.
- **Test a pre-release from its own catalog image**,
  `ghcr.io/redhat-na-ssa/openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator-catalog:v<VERSION>`, for example `:v0.3.0-rc2`. A
  pre-release does not move `:latest`, and `:latest` does not exist until the first final release.
- **Re-running the workflow publishes the version again.** The bundle gets a new digest, the image tags are
  overwritten and `release/<tag>` is replaced. The tagged commit does not have the catalog entry that was merged
  later, so after the merge a re-run builds a second catalog update for the same version, which conflicts with the
  merged one. Do not re-run a release whose pull request is merged; release a new version instead.
- **The bundle directory is not kept.** `bundles/<VERSION>/` is git-ignored and the workflow's workspace is discarded.
  For the community catalogs, regenerate the bundle at the tag with `make bundle`, or extract it from the pushed bundle
  image. Neither way is scripted or tested here.

**By hand:**

1. Set `IMAGE_TAG_BASE` (in `.envrc`) and log in to that registry. Check the version in `.envrc`. It must not be in
   `catalog-template.yaml` yet.
2. Run `make release`. It runs `release-check`, then:
   - builds and pushes the operator image;
   - generates the bundle, which pins the operator image by digest when `USE_IMAGE_DIGESTS=true`, then builds and
     pushes the bundle image;
   - `catalog-add` makes the bundle the new channel head, with `replaces` set to the old head and
     `skipRange: >=0.3.0-rc2 <VERSION` (0.3.0-rc2 is the first version released with the current API group, see
     `CATALOG_SKIP_FROM`);
   - `catalog-render` pulls every bundle image and takes a few minutes;
   - builds and pushes the catalog image, and tags all three images as `:latest` (not for a pre-release, a `VERSION`
     with a `-` such as `0.3.0-rc2`).
3. Commit `catalog-template.yaml` and `catalog/`.
4. Update the docs for the new version, as in [After each release](#after-each-release).
5. Run `make increment` to bump `PATCH` in `.envrc`, then commit it (not after a pre-release).

`make release` records the bundle in the catalog by tag (`BUNDLE_IMG`) and refuses any other `BUNDLE_REF`. The
bundle's digest is only known once it is pushed, because every `make bundle` writes a new `createdAt`. To record the
bundle by digest instead, run the steps of `make release` one at a time and read the digest of the pushed bundle in
between, for example with skopeo, which uses the podman or docker login:

```sh
make release-check
make docker-build docker-push
make bundle
make bundle-build bundle-push
digest=$(skopeo inspect --format '{{.Digest}}' docker://<IMAGE_TAG_BASE>-bundle:v<VERSION>)
make catalog-add BUNDLE_REF=<IMAGE_TAG_BASE>-bundle@$digest
make catalog-render
make catalog-build catalog-push
make latest
```

`skopeo` prints the full digest, `sha256:...`, so `BUNDLE_REF` gets no second `sha256:` prefix. `catalog-add` does
not check the format of the reference, and running it again for the same version is refused. To undo a wrong
`catalog-add`, run `git checkout catalog-template.yaml` (and `git checkout catalog/` if `catalog-render` already ran),
then run it again. Then continue with steps 3 to 5.

To publish in the community catalogs, copy the bundle (`manifests/`, `metadata/` and `tests/`) into
`operators/openshift-node-upgrade-mutex-operator/<VERSION>/` of a fork of
[k8s-operatorhub/community-operators](https://github.com/k8s-operatorhub/community-operators) or
[redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod](https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod),
and open a pull request. Those catalogs hold 0.2.x, under the old API group, in the channel `alpha`. Publish 0.3.0
there only in a new channel (set `CHANNELS` and `DEFAULT_CHANNEL` for `make bundle`), or 0.2.x installs would be
offered an upgrade to an API that ignores their CRs. [HANDOFF.md](docs/HANDOFF.md) lists this as a decision for the
owner.

#### After each release

Once the `release/<tag>` pull request is merged, update the docs for the new version in a pull request:

1. `sample-manifests/catalogsource.yaml`: the tag in `spec.image` and the comment that names it. Use the newest final
   release, or the newest pre-release while there is no final release.
2. `docs/USAGE.md`:
   - the `Releases` row of the table at the top;
   - [Catalog and versions](docs/USAGE.md#catalog-and-versions): what the project's catalog offers, the tag the sample
     CatalogSource uses and, after the first final release, that `:latest` exists;
   - [Tested environments](docs/USAGE.md#tested-environments), if the release ran on a live cluster, together with
     [tests/Scenarios.md](tests/Scenarios.md).
3. Any other text that names the previous release's tag or says that nothing is released yet. While the docs name
   `0.3.0-rc2`, this finds both; change the version in it once they name another:
   `git grep -n -e '0\.3\.0-rc2' -e 'first release' -e 'no release yet' -- docs/USAGE.md sample-manifests/`
4. `make document`, then commit `README.md` and the CSV base with the change.

A release's CSV description is `docs/USAGE.md` at its tag, so the console shows these updates from the next release
on. Word the release state in USAGE so that it also reads correctly at the tag, as the `Releases` row and Catalog and
versions do now: "The first release there is 0.3.0-rc2; until it is published, the catalog is empty".

### Making a change

What to update with each kind of change. The pull request template has the same list as checkboxes, and
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) links here.

**A role or a task file:**

- Update the role's README, and [DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) when a gate, an annotation, an invariant or an MCO
  assumption changes.
- Update the reconcile procedure, the conditions and the troubleshooting in `docs/USAGE.md` when users see the
  change, then run `make document`.
- Add or change the molecule assertions (`molecule/default/tasks/`), and update
  [tests/Scenarios.md](tests/Scenarios.md).
- `make lint`, and the E2E check on the pull request.

**A CRD field:**

- `config/crd/bases/`, and the matching `specDescriptors` in the CSV base.
- The role that validates or reads it, and `config/samples/` if the samples should show it.
- The field tables in `docs/USAGE.md`, then `make document`.
- `make bundle bundle-validate verify-manifests`.

**Permissions:**

- `config/rbac/role.yaml` is least privilege: every rule maps to a call in `roles/` or in ansible-operator itself.
  Add a new resource or verb there.
- Add it to the permissions table in `docs/USAGE.md` (the metrics rules come from
  `config/rbac/metrics_auth_role.yaml`), then `make document`.
- `make bundle verify-manifests`.

**Defaults and timings:**

- `roles/mutexrunconfig/defaults/main.yml`, and the defaults table in its README.
- The timings in `docs/USAGE.md` and, for the settle time, [DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).
- The molecule timeouts, if the tests wait on the value.

**A condition reason or message:**

- The conditions and troubleshooting in `docs/USAGE.md`; nothing else may quote the old text.
- `git grep` the old reason in `molecule/` and fix the assertions.

**Documentation:**

- The rules under Documentation and diagrams, then `make docs-lint`.
- `make document` after a change to `docs/USAGE.md` or this file, and `make diagrams` after a change to a `.mmd`.

### Bumping the toolchain

Each pin lives in the places below. Bump them together and run CI.

| Tool | Pinned in |
| --- | --- |
| ansible-operator, operator-sdk and the scorecard image (v1.42.3) | `Dockerfile`, `Makefile` (`OPERATOR_SDK_VERSION`), `config/scorecard/patches/*.yaml`; mentioned in `roles/*/meta/main.yml`, `roles/*/README.md`, `requirements.yml`, `molecule/requirements.txt`, `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` and this file. `git grep -n 'v1\.42\.3'` finds them. |
| ansible-core (2.18.18, the version in the ansible-operator image) | `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `molecule/requirements.txt` |
| yamllint, ansible-lint | `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` |
| molecule, the Python kubernetes client | `molecule/requirements.txt` |
| collections `operator_sdk.util`, `kubernetes.core` | `requirements.yml` |
| kustomize, yq | `Makefile`; the kustomize path in `molecule/README.md` and in the molecule recipe above |
| opm | both `FROM` lines of `catalog.Dockerfile` |
| kind | `.github/workflows/e2e.yaml` (`KIND_VERSION` and `KIND_SHA256`) |
| GitHub Actions | the commit SHAs in `.github/workflows/*.yaml` |
| Python for the workflows (3.12) | `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `.github/workflows/e2e.yaml` |
| mermaid-cli | `MMDC_IMG` in the Makefile; then `make diagrams` (see Documentation and diagrams) |

The OpenShift version range is a pin too: `custom-annotations.yaml` (`com.redhat.openshift.versions: v4.16`) and
`spec.minKubeVersion` in the CSV base (`1.29.0`) must move together.

See [HANDOFF.md](docs/HANDOFF.md) for where the repository, its images and its catalog live, and what is left for its owner.
